blank.structure: Template only. A shipping plugin must declare its mod root or package format and the file layout users should install or edit.
blank.overriding: Template only. A shipping plugin must declare whether mods stack, replace whole files, merge semantic records, or are mutually exclusive.

ff7.loader: FFNx Direct Mode. Lexeditor can build an isolated Direct Mode export, deploy to an existing FFNx.toml, or install the pinned upstream FFNx-v1.24.3.0 release for the classic 2026 Steam layout. The archive is SHA-256 verified and manual/7th-Heaven FFNx installs remain externally owned.
ff7.structure: Lexeditor project saves remain outside the game. Export writes .lexeditor/ffnx-direct plus an ownership manifest. Deploy maps only proved KERNEL/KERNEL2 chunks, scene blocks, field encounter section 7 and world enc_w.bin into FFNx's configured direct_mode_path. Executable-backed edits remain project-only.
ff7.overriding: Lexeditor owns only files listed in .lexeditor-ff7.json and refuses pre-existing unowned Direct Mode paths. Updates/removal require the deployed file hash to match the prior manifest. An opt-in read-only 7th Heaven profile/folder scan reports active ordered mods and blocks definite same-path Direct overlaps; conditional roots and .iro packages remain explicitly incomplete rather than guessed.

ff7-2013.loader: Not implemented. Lexeditor currently edits safe project copies and does not deploy or load mods into the 2013 PC release.
ff7-2013.structure: One selected Lexeditor project mirrors supported game-relative paths, including data/lang-en/kernel/KERNEL.BIN, outside the installed game.
ff7-2013.overriding: No runtime mod stack exists yet. Lexeditor edits one project at a time; multiple FFVII 2013 mods are not composed or resolved by priority.

ff7r.loader: Lexeditor supports two guarded PAK paths for FF7R. Build & Deploy writes one ownership-marked Lexeditor-FF7R_P.pak; Mod Library imports PAK folders/ZIPs and deploys enabled packages only under ~mods/LexeditorLibrary. Runtime-only features use the separate NativeMods path.
ff7r.structure: Installed game archives stay read-only. Project edits live under the selected project's content/ tree and build into <project>/build/. Mod Library keeps imported packages outside the game, then copies enabled PAKs into its owned LexeditorLibrary subfolder under End/Content/Paks/~mods.
ff7r.overriding: Lexeditor does not semantically merge separate PAK mods or guess a load-order winner. Mod Library and direct project deployment inspect PAK indexes and refuse exact game-asset collisions with another active PAK. Non-overlapping PAKs coexist; ownership hashes prevent replacement/removal of unmanaged or externally changed Lexeditor deployments.

ff8.loader: De novo Lexeditor pre-launch compositor targeting FFNx. It reads Junction VIII-compatible mod.xml folder metadata and imports .iroj packages, but does not adopt Junction's live load model.
ff8.structure: Managed mods go in %LOCALAPPDATA%\Lexeditor\mods\ff8\<mod>\ or can be imported as .iroj packages. Folder mods use mod.json for Lexeditor metadata and may contain direct/, hext/, textures/, sfx/, voice/, ambient/, override/, and save/ roots; optional mod.xml supplies Junction-style folder options.
ff8.overriding: Enabled mods compose from low to high priority. Same-path ordinary files are higher-priority-wins and Hext patches are ordered; supported packed gameplay data such as kernel.bin is semantically merged against vanilla so non-overlapping record or field edits coexist, while overlapping semantic edits conflict and the higher-priority edit wins.

ff9.loader: Memoria. Its Mod Manager installs, enables and removes external FF9 mods; Lexeditor deploys only its marker-owned Lexeditor mod folder and hands external-mod management to Memoria's launcher. Mods declaring a MinimumMemoriaVersion newer than Lexeditor's pinned v2025.07.04 are unsupported until the helper pin is deliberately updated and re-verified.
ff9.structure: Lexeditor projects contain game-relative overrides under StreamingAssets/ plus Lexeditor-owned feature configuration. Deploy copies only those overrides and the Lexeditor runtime into <FF9>/Lexeditor. Other Memoria mod folders and installed p0data archives are not rewritten.
ff9.overriding: Memoria runtime priority is FolderNames order, highest priority first. Lexeditor deploy keeps Lexeditor first there and, when Priorities already exists, first in that launcher list too; it does not invent a missing Priorities setting. Lexeditor-generated CSV, battle raw16 and field-walkmesh BGI replacements are first-hit whole-file overrides. Format-specific Memoria patch files may compose low-to-high, and event scripts have separate append/MergeScripts behavior. Lexeditor does not claim a universal semantic merge between separate mods.

palworld.loader: Pocketpair's official Palworld v0.7+ mod loader and Workshop package model. Lexeditor authors compatible packages and PalSchema raw-table patches, builds a clean snapshot, can create one owned unregistered client test package, and can stage/activate a server-compatible package for the Windows dedicated server. Client activation remains read-only; dedicated-server activation is an explicit stale-guarded reversible PalModSettings.ini transaction. Lexeditor does not publish to Steam or install/replace PalSchema or UE4SS.
palworld.structure: One selected Lexeditor project is rooted at Info.json. Build Package creates <project>/build/official-package from Info.json, Thumbnail and declared InstallRule targets while excluding Lexeditor recovery artifacts. Client local testing uses one owned random 10-digit folder under workshop/content/1623730. Server deployment requires IsServer=true and uses <PalServer>/Mods/Workshop/Lexeditor-<PackageName>; server activation recovery state stays under the project, never inside the package.
palworld.overriding: The official loader identifies packages by PackageName. Lexeditor refuses client or server deployment when another source folder already uses the same PackageName and refuses to overwrite externally modified owned state. PalSchema raw patches apply named DataTable row/property values rather than whole assets; when several runtime patches target the same field, Lexeditor does not claim a separate conflict winner beyond PalSchema's runtime order.

rdr.loader: Archive-backed RDR1 project replacements deploy through Ultimate ASI Loader's update-folder overload mechanism. RedHook is a separate external runtime prerequisite for Lexeditor's runtime/plugin features; Lexeditor does not bundle either third-party runtime.
rdr.structure: Lexeditor edits one project (C:\RDRMod by default); archive-relative replacements live under <project>\mod\. Deploy Project rebuilds only affected RPF6 copies under <RDR>\update\game\... while leaving installed source archives untouched. External RedHook .red plugins remain separate files in the game root.
rdr.overriding: Lexeditor has one active archive deployment, not a multi-mod priority stack. Root RedHook .red and ASI files are left untouched and can remain side-by-side on disk, but runtime coexistence is not claimed. A whole-archive mod that also owns update/game/<archive>.rpf conflicts at that exact path: Lexeditor does not semantically merge it, preserves/restores the pre-existing archive while it owns deployment, and refuses to overwrite an externally changed deployed archive. The public rpf_patch.asi loader documents patch0.rpf, patch1.rpf, ... with higher numbers overriding lower ones; Lexeditor does not import, create, reorder, or verify that runtime priority.

rdr2.loader: Lenny's Mod Loader (LML) EasyInstall package format. Lexeditor edits an LML package but does not fork, bundle, or replace LML's runtime or Mod Manager.
rdr2.structure: Lexeditor edits one EasyInstall folder (C:\RDR2Mod\MyOverhaul by default) whose install.xml maps each GamePath to a package FilePath. To run it with LML, place or copy the whole install.xml mod folder under <RDR2>\lml\<mod>\.
rdr2.overriding: LML owns enabled state and load order. If separate LML packages replace the same GamePath, the later/higher-priority replacement wins as a complete file; Lexeditor does not semantically merge records across separate LML mods.

warband.loader: Warband's native module system. WSE2 is Lexeditor's optional enhanced runtime helper, not a multi-mod overlay loader.
warband.structure: Each installed mod is its own folder under <Warband>\Modules\ with module.ini. Lexeditor can also edit and build a Module System source project before it becomes an installed module.
warband.overriding: Warband selects one module at launch. Lexeditor does not stack several modules or apply a cross-module priority order; resources and dependencies declared by the selected module follow Warband's own module rules.

ff7r2.loader: Two loaders sit beside ff7rebirth_.exe in End/Binaries/Win64, each under a name Windows loads for the game. ReShade is dxgi.dll. Shader Injector 2.2.1 is dsound.dll, with its ShaderInjector folder, and replaces the game's own lighting, shadow, water and post-process shaders while it runs. Rebirth's own d3d12.dll, or a DirectX 12 fix installed under that name, is never overwritten.
ff7r2.structure: A Rebirth project holds a reshade/ folder with the preset .ini and any shaders its author wrote. Shader Injector ships inside Lexeditor as upstream's pinned release archive and is extracted into the game folder on request; ShaderInjector.ini beside the executable holds its settings, and the ShaderInjector folder holds the shaders people edit.
ff7r2.overriding: ReShade applies one preset at a time over the finished frame. Shader Injector changes shaders before that, so the two stack rather than compete. Files the player has edited in the ShaderInjector folder are kept on reinstall and removal, and a PAK mod from elsewhere is untouched.
